title: Scroll the selected case into view
description: public/ has no scrollIntoView call anywhere (grep, 2026-09-13). With 625 cases j walks the selection off the bottom of the pane and the user sees nothing move. The old portal called box.scrollIntoView({block:'nearest'}). Apply the same to the selected row after every selection change, from key and from click.

title: Fix j and k losing keystrokes and jumping back to the first case
description: Seen live at 127.0.0.1:4180 with 625 cases: 14 quick presses of j left the selection on the first case. Cause: public/app.js selectCase() awaits GET /api/cases/:id/history before it calls setState, so every key pressed during the fetch reads a stale state.selectedId. When selectedId is still null the index is -1 and ids[min(0, ...)] returns the first row. Fix: set the selection synchronously on the key event, then load history after, and drop a history response that is no longer for the selected case. The old portal moved the selection with no network call at all (move(1) / move(-1)).

title: Dashboard parity: buttons, keyboard and visual language
description: The owner tested qa-desk on a case set of 625 cases and found the controls and keyboard of the earlier in-house QA portal missing. That portal is the tool qa-desk generalises, and its single page UI was inventoried on 2026-09-13 as the parity reference. Three defects were also found in a live check of the running UI. This epic holds the defects, the missing controls, the keyboard set and the visual language. It does not hold reports or suites, which stay in phase 3 and phase 4.

title: Show the keys on screen: key caps and a footer legend
description: The only place qa-desk names its keys is the empty state text of the detail pane, which disappears as soon as a case is selected. The old portal printed a key cap inside each verdict button and kept a legend in the footer at all times: j k move, p f b s verdict, Enter comment, Esc leave field. Add a ? overlay that lists every key once the set grows.

title: Add the missing keys: arrows, Enter and Escape
description: qa-desk binds j, k and the five verdict keys only. The old portal also bound ArrowDown and ArrowUp as aliases of j and k, Enter to focus and scroll to the comment box, and Escape to blur the current field, with Escape checked before the is-typing guard so it can free a select or the search box. Keep the existing rule that any of Meta, Ctrl or Alt aborts the handler.

title: Show a header tally and progress without a run
description: The Cases header says only Cases (625), and the progress pane says Pick a run to see progress, so a user with no open run sees no numbers at all. The old portal always showed a tally of visible against total plus marked, pass and fail counts, and one stacked progress bar per group with a spoken aria-label for the breakdown.

title: Complete the fix agent panel: model picker, log toggle, auto refresh
description: qa-desk has Dispatch fix agent and Refresh, and shows a log only from the dispatch made in the same page session. The old portal had a model select beside Dispatch, a Show log and Hide log toggle that fetched the log on demand, a Dispatch again label after a failed dispatch, a 5 second reload that ran only while some dispatch was running, and a 15 second poll of the tracker issue while the case stayed selected.

title: Show a save state for the free text fields and flush on page exit
description: The Actual result and Evidence boxes save on blur only. Text typed and then lost to a closed tab is gone with no warning, and nothing on screen says whether the last edit reached the server. The old portal debounced the save at 600 ms, showed Not saved yet, then Saving, then Saved HH:MM:SS, then Not saved. Edit again to retry., flushed on blur, and fired a keepalive PUT on pagehide. It also kept the text the user was typing when a background refresh arrived.

title: Show a connection indicator and an error banner the user can dismiss
description: qa-desk reports every failure as a toast in the top bar that hides itself after 6 seconds and cannot be dismissed or recalled. The old portal had a footer dot that flipped between Connected and Server not responding the moment a fetch threw, a banner with an explicit Dismiss button and an 8 second auto clear, and offline copy that named the command to restart the server.

title: Give every empty state an action button
description: qa-desk shows plain text: Loading, No cases match, and the boot error. The old portal had three distinct empty states, each with its own action: a load error with Retry, an empty case file with Reload and the exact merge command to run, and a filtered-to-nothing state with Clear filters.

title: Add a Clear filters button and remember filters between reloads
description: qa-desk has 10 filter selects and a search box and no way to reset them but to set each back to All, and every filter is lost on reload. The old portal had a Clear link beside the Filters heading that stayed hidden while no filter was set, saved all filters plus the search text to localStorage under one key, read them on load, and silently reset any saved value that no longer exists in the current case set.

title: Stop rebuilding every case row on each keystroke
description: render() calls root.replaceChildren() and renderList maps every visible case to new DOM nodes. With 625 cases every character typed in the search box rebuilds the whole list, because the search input has no debounce. The old portal debounced search at 140 ms and kept a pool of row nodes it refilled in place; its own comment measured about 350 ms to rebuild about 900 rows against a fraction of that to refill. Add the debounce first, then row reuse.

title: Support right to left text in case content
description: Case titles, steps and free text are rendered with no direction hint, so an Arabic title inside the English chrome breaks up. The old portal set dir=auto on titles and list items and used unicode-bidi: plaintext on the title cell. This matters for the client work the tool is aimed at.

title: Polish the layout: sticky detail head, breakpoints, monospace ids
description: The detail pane scrolls its own title away, the grid has one breakpoint at 1000px that stacks all three columns at once, and case ids are set in a proportional font so they do not line up. The old portal pinned the detail header, moved to two columns at 1100px and one at 760px while hiding the least useful column first, set ids and counts in tabular monospace, and flattened every animation under prefers-reduced-motion.

title: Add the icon set: favicon, search, chevron, external link
description: qa-desk ships no icon of any kind and no favicon, so the browser tab shows the default globe. The old portal stayed dependency free and still had three inline SVG glyphs: a search magnifier in the search box, a chevron baked into the selects as a data URI, and a small external link arrow on the pull request link. Inline SVG only, no icon font and no network request.

title: Add colour chips for priority, severity, type and tags
description: Every case row prints one grey meta line, so a P0 critical row looks exactly like a P2 minor row across 625 rows, and the only colour on the Cases screen is the blue accent. The old portal used pill chips with their own colour for priority P0 to P3, for kind, for the tracker issue and for the dispatch state, and used a 9px dot for the verdict instead of a wide uppercase badge. Keep the verdict colours qa-desk already has.

title: Add an undo key for the last verdict
description: New, not parity. A verdict key writes an execution the moment it is pressed, and a mis-keyed p is only correctable by pressing the right key again, which leaves the wrong verdict in the run history. Bind u to revert the last execution the current session recorded, and say what it reverted.

title: Warn when the selected case is hidden by the current filters
description: Select a case, then set a filter that excludes it: qa-desk keeps the detail on screen with no row to match it. The old portal showed an inline warning in the detail header that said the case is hidden by the current filters.
